sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (December 1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 1 'Special Relativity' printed pp. 28-30 (PDF pp. 35-37): the energy-momentum tensors of dust and a perfect fluid. Ch. 4 'Gravitation' printed pp. 116-118 (PDF pp. 123-125): the field equations from the action, the Hilbert stress-energy tensor and the Weak Energy Condition (4.72) as an extra assumption. Ch. 5 'More Geometry' printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149): Killing vectors (5.39)-(5.42), the Killing equation and the conserved quantity along geodesics.

contents.name: Ch. 1 (1.104)-(1.110) printed pp. 28-30: dust T^{mu nu} = rho U^mu U^nu and perfect-fluid T^{mu nu} = (rho+p)U^mu U^nu + p eta^{mu nu}, with the component readings
contents.support: The static dust tensor T = rho u (x) u used in the example is the pressureless case of the source tensor; the example's own identities are proved from the framework's dust model and the flat chart.

contents.name: Ch. 4 printed pp. 116-118: the field equations as the variation of the action and T_{mu nu} = -(1/sqrt(-g)) delta S_M/delta g^{mu nu}, with the Weak Energy Condition (4.72) stated as a separate assumption
contents.support: The counterexample's point that conservation and pointwise nonnegativity are independent conditions is exactly the source's separation of the energy condition from the field equations and conservation; the computation itself is local.

contents.name: Ch. 5 (5.39)-(5.42) printed pp. 140-142: Killing vectors, L_X g = 0 and nabla_mu X_nu + nabla_nu X_mu = 0, and the conserved quantity along geodesics
contents.support: The Killing equation used to reduce the symmetric part of nabla n and to identify the gradient of the normalization is this source's Killing equation; the lemma proves the congruence identities locally.

contents.name: Ch. 5 (5.39)-(5.42) printed pp. 140-142, energy/momentum interpretation of the conserved Killing contraction for a timelike Killing vector
contents.support: The definition's reading of Q_xi as the model's energy follows the source's identification of the conserved charge with the energy of matter for timelike Killing vectors; the definition itself is stated in the framework's own current and flux language.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), 125 PDF pages
sources.locator: Section 5.3 printed pp. 53-56 (PDF pp. 54-57): Lie derivative, Killing vectors and conserved quantities. Section 7.5 printed pp. 88-89 (PDF pp. 89-90): the energy in gravitational waves, the non-gauge-invariance of the quadratic tensor t_{mu nu}, the statement that gravitational energy cannot be localized, and the ADM energy as a surface integral at infinity. Section 8.7 printed pp. 109-110 (PDF pp. 110-111): Stokes' theorem and flux balance. Section 9.3 printed pp. 116-118 (PDF pp. 117-119): the energy-momentum tensor and on-shell conservation nabla_a T^{ab} = 0.

contents.name: Section 5.3 printed pp. 53-56: Killing vectors defined by L_X g = 0, the equivalent equation and the conserved quantity X_a V^a along geodesics
contents.support: Shared prerequisite context supplied by the Einstein-and-matter page: the Killing equation and its consequences are absorbed into the page's Killing-congruence lemma and Killing energy charge, which restate the exact clauses they use.

contents.name: Section 7.5 printed pp. 88-89: t_{mu nu} quadratic in h is not invariant under gauge transformations; 'the impossibility of localizing gravitational energy'; the integral of t_{00} over a constant-time surface is gauge invariant under decay at infinity and defines the ADM energy
contents.support: Direct support for the remark's scope statements that no gauge-invariant local gravitational energy density is available and that asymptotic masses require additional structure; the remark states the framework's scope, not a no-go theorem.

contents.name: Section 8.7 printed pp. 109-110: Stokes' theorem and the flux balance on a region bounded by two spacelike slices and a timelike boundary
contents.support: The finite-chain balance identity of the lemma is the framework's version of this source's flux balance, applied to the measured energy-momentum current.

contents.name: Section 9.3 printed pp. 116-118: T^{ab} from the matter action and nabla_a T^{ab} = 0 on shell
contents.support: The theorem's clause (a) is the framework's version of this on-shell conservation statement, supplied by the Einstein-and-matter consistency theorem.

sources.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), 289 PDF pages
sources.locator: Section 4.3.2 printed p. 163 (PDF p. 170): symmetries and conserved quantities, and the de Sitter discussion in which the Killing field is timelike only in the static patch and there is no global positive conserved energy. Section 4.3.3 printed pp. 165-167 (PDF pp. 172-174): Komar integrals and their interpretation as the mass of the spacetime. Sections 4.5.3-4.5.4 printed pp. 183-187 (PDF pp. 190-194): the dust and perfect-fluid tensors and the equations equivalent to their conservation. Section 4.5.5 printed pp. 187-189 (PDF pp. 194-196): 'The Slippery Business of Energy Conservation', charge conservation in curved spacetime, the failure of covariant conservation of T to give actual conservation, and the conserved charge of the Killing current -K^mu T_{mu nu}. Section 4.5.7 printed pp. 194-198 (PDF pp. 201-205): the energy conditions as assumptions on T.

contents.name: Section 4.3.2 printed p. 163: de Sitter's Killing field is timelike only in part of the spacetime, so there is no global positive conserved energy
contents.support: Supports the remark's statement that a Killing field need not be timelike everywhere and that a global energy requires more than the existence of a Killing field; the remark records this as scope, not as a theorem.

contents.name: Section 4.3.3 printed pp. 165-167: Komar integrals, d star F = 0 in vacuum and the identification of the Komar charge with the mass of the spacetime
contents.reason: The framework's current pages define no asymptotic or boundary structure, and the design defers ADM/Komar-type masses to a boundary-asymptotic module that is not a declared page of this run's plan; no Komar integral is defined, computed or used by this batch.

contents.name: Sections 4.5.3-4.5.4 printed pp. 183-187: the perfect-fluid tensor (4.53) and the conservation equations (4.54)-(4.55) as the energy equation and the Euler equation
contents.support: The recovered equation D epsilon + (epsilon+p) theta = 0 is exactly the source's equation (4.54); the example derives it from the page's local balance instead of from a direct divergence computation.

contents.name: Section 4.5.5 printed pp. 187-189: charge conservation in curved spacetime and the role of the side flux; covariant conservation of T is not actual conservation; the current J_T = -K^mu T_{mu nu} is conserved for Killing K and its charge is the energy of the matter for timelike K
contents.support: The theorem's balance and stationary-conservation clauses are the framework's exact form of these statements, with the finite-chain flux hypotheses made explicit.

contents.name: Section 4.5.5 printed pp. 188-189: the charge Q_T(Sigma) of the Killing current and its energy interpretation for a timelike Killing vector
contents.support: Supplies the reading of the Killing current and its flux as the model's energy assigned to a chain; the definition fixes the normalization and the finite-chain domain.

contents.name: Section 4.5.7 printed pp. 194-198: the four energy conditions as additional assumptions on the stress-energy tensor
contents.support: Confirms that pointwise positivity of the measured energy density is an extra assumption rather than a consequence of conservation; the counterexample exhibits a divergence-free tensor violating it.

sources.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), 220 PDF pages
sources.locator: Sections 3.3.3-3.3.4 printed pp. 42-44 (PDF pp. 42-44): Eulerian observers, their 4-acceleration a = grad_n n = D ln N and the decomposition grad n = -K - D ln N (x) n. Section 4.1.2 printed p. 52 (PDF p. 52): the 3+1 decomposition of the stress-energy tensor, E = T(n,n), p = -T(n,gamma(.)) and S = gamma*T as measured by the Eulerian observer. Section 5.2 printed pp. 72-74 (PDF pp. 72-74): energy and momentum conservation in 3+1 form, the energy equation with the expansion term, the remark that p is both the momentum density and the energy flux, and the Newtonian limit. Chapter 4 section 4.5 printed pp. 65-70 (PDF pp. 65-70): the ADM Hamiltonian formulation.

contents.name: Sections 3.3.3-3.3.4 printed pp. 42-44: the Eulerian observer congruence, its 4-acceleration a = grad_n n and the identity a = D ln N
contents.support: Supplies the standard geometric content of the acceleration field of an observer congruence and the acceleration-as-gradient identity; the item defines the objects intrinsically with the metric-selected connection.

contents.name: Sections 3.3.3-3.3.4 printed pp. 42-44: spatiality of the acceleration and its expression through the gradient of the lapse
contents.support: The lemma proves the spatiality and the curve identity of the acceleration for an arbitrary congruence and the divergence form of the expansion, of which the source's Eulerian case is the foliation-adapted instance.

contents.name: Section 4.1.2 printed p. 52: E = T(n,n) is the energy density measured by the Eulerian observer, p = -T(n,gamma(.)) the momentum density and S = gamma*T the stress
contents.support: Supplies the decomposition pattern mu, Phi, S of the measured fields for an observer congruence; the item states it for an arbitrary smooth symmetric T and proves the identities.

contents.name: Section 4.1.2 printed p. 52 and section 5.2.3 printed p. 74: the measured energy density, momentum density and stress, and the remark that p plays the role of an energy flux and that both aspects are equivalent
contents.support: Supplies the physical reading of the measured fields, including the identification of the energy-flux and momentum-density readings of one component; the item fixes the framework's component and unit conventions.

contents.name: Section 5.2.1-5.2.2 printed pp. 72-73: the 3+1 decomposition of nabla_mu T^{mu nu} = 0 and the energy conservation equation containing the expansion term
contents.support: The lemma's balance identity D mu + mu theta + div Phi = -T^{ab} nabla_a n_b is the intrinsic form of this source's projected conservation equation; the lemma proves it for arbitrary congruences and manifolds.

contents.name: Section 5.2.3 printed pp. 73-74: the Newtonian limit of the energy equation and the gravitational power source -p . D Phi
contents.support: The example's nonvanishing-density balance with a conserved measured current is the flat, non-gravitational counterpart of the source's discussion of source terms and flux; no Newtonian limit is claimed by the example.

contents.name: Chapter 4 section 4.5 printed pp. 65-70: the ADM Hamiltonian formulation and the ADM mass
contents.reason: The design defers ADM-type masses to a boundary-asymptotic module that is not a declared page of this run's plan; the batch defines no initial-data or asymptotic structure and uses no ADM quantity.
